sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes a partial skeleton with a full skull but lacks most hindlimbs.
Its face features two extra openings behind the nostril that line up with the nose's center.
The defensive tail club viewed from above is hexagonal, with its widest section near the back edge.
This animal holds the record as the most primitive ankylosaur known to have a proper tail club.
It replaced Pinacosaurus as the earliest known dinosaur to possess this specific defensive weapon.
Fossils of this species represent the southernmost ankylosaurid discovery in Asia.
A farmer found the remains at a construction site in Jinyun County, China, during June 2008.
Six researchers formally named and described the species Jinyunpelta sinensis in 2018.
Studies suggest this creature used biphasal jaw movement, a trait thought to appear later in ankylosaurid evolution.
In 2018, scientists placed the animal in the subfamily Ankylosaurinae within the family Ankylosauridae.
This dinosaur lived between 100 and 95 million years ago during the Albian to Cenomanian stages of the Cretaceous.
Its specific time range is recorded as the Albian stage, spanning from 113.2 to 100.5 million years ago.
